source.text:
09-CRO / testing and experiments

Goes here. Gathering qualitative and quantitative behavioral data to formulate test hypotheses. Heatmaps, session recordings, area maps, user testing platforms, and on-site surveys. Specifically capturing the feature comparisons between Microsoft Clarity and Hotjar, the unbundled tech stack alternatives for user testing and surveys, and how to use area map click data to design A/B tests.

Not here.

Setting up custom event funnels and path explorations in Google Analytics 4 -> 06-MEA

Post-purchase survey setups for marketing attribution -> 06-MEA

Redesigning the landing page UI or changing copywriting based on the data -> 07-LPG

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Breaks down the exact feature differences between Microsoft Clarity and Hotjar, providing a cost-effective, unbundled tech stack (Clarity + Userbrain + Okendo + GA4) for CRO research. modules: [CRO] topics: [test design] tier: 3 scope_hint: baseline

Topics. test design / Utilizing "Area Maps" (Microsoft Clarity) to see exact click percentages on specific elements (e.g., lower-page icons) to formulate A/B test hypotheses, as opposed to relying on broader "Engagement Zones" (Hotjar). qualitative tools / Building a cost-effective CRO research stack by unbundling Hotjar's premium features: using Microsoft Clarity for free, unlimited heatmaps and session recordings; Userbrain for remote user testing interviews; Okendo for unlimited on-site and post-purchase Shopify surveys; and Google Analytics 4 (Explore tab) for custom navigation funnels.

Look for. The specific A/B test framework example: using Clarity Area Maps to identify that 10.41% of clicks went to a "shop by industry" section that only 30-35% of people actually reached, and moving those elements to the top of the homepage to achieve an 18% conversion lift. The specific tool alternatives to bypass Hotjar's expensive pricing tiers: Microsoft Clarity (Free heatmaps/recordings), Okendo (unlimited Shopify surveys tied to order data), Userbrain ($40/tester for remote user interviews), and GA4 (Custom funnels via the Explore tab).

Skip. Basic definitions of what heatmaps, session recordings, or exit-intent surveys are. General complaints about tool pricing without the specific dollar amounts or session limits (e.g., Hotjar's $32/month for 100 daily sessions).

Scope mix. Almost all baseline.

Volume. 10 to 15.
